Submission Instructions

  1. Select a 10-sentence section of your primary witness text and an authoritative modern translation.
  2. Align the sentences into parallel pairs (assigning xml:id="s1", xml:id="s2" ... to source sentences, and xml:id="t1", xml:id="t2" ... to target translation sentences).
  3. For 3 sentences, construct a full four-line Leipzig Interlinear Gloss: (Line 1: Source text, Line 2: Morpheme segmentation, Line 3: Grammatical gloss with capitalized category tags, Line 4: Free idiomatic translation).
  4. Encode the entire alignment in a TEI XML document utilizing a stand-off <linkGrp type="translation-alignment"><link target="#s1 #t1"/>...</linkGrp> structure.
  5. Submit your TEI XML file and a 300–500 word reflection discussing the challenge of non-isomorphic syntactic alignment (where one word in language A requires a multi-word phrase in language B).
